Maria Chen: Quick follow-up from the RFC — ran a sim sweep of the current fallback ordering. Under peak load high-tier tenants keep >99.9% success while low-tier served_fraction drops ~2-3x compared to baseline. We didn't explicitly surface a fairness metric in the RFC; is this acceptable or do we need a stronger guarantee?

Ajay Patel: Not acceptable for some customers. We need to be explicit: SLO for paying tiers + a fairness floor for all tenants. Proposal sketch: define a 'min_served_fraction' per tier over a rolling window and a 'bias_cap' that limits how much priority can skew selection.

Simon Loe: A couple of patterns to consider: 1) hard quotas (guaranteed min share) — simple but can reduce overall throughput; 2) weighted randomized selection — preserves throughput and avoids starvation but is probabilistic; 3) priority decay — if a tenant is prioritized repeatedly, temporarily down-weight them.

Nina Ortega: I like weighted-rand + guardrails. That keeps tail latency lower than strict quotas. But we need to protect enterprise customers: a soft-SLA that promotes them when their served_fraction drops near their SLO threshold.

policy-bot: sim-run-1785554321: results uploaded to /internal/sims/fallback-bias-1785554321. TL;DR: weighted_randomization reduces starvation events by ~40% for low-tier under our synthetic spikes, at cost of ~5% throughput drop. Hard quotas cut throughput ~18% but eliminate starvation almost entirely.

Maria Chen: What about a hybrid algorithm: priority-biased reservoir sampling with tenant-level min shares enforced as soft guarantees. Pseudocode: 
```
# on request arrival:
score = priority_weight * base_score - bias_cap_adjustment
choose tenant via reservoir_sample(weight=exp(score))
if tenant.served_fraction < tenant.min_share: boost weight by min_share_boost
```
This keeps bias but nudges sampling when a tenant falls behind.

Ajay Patel: Implementation notes: we need per-pool reservoir samplers (hot path), atomic served_fraction counters (redis or memcache with accurate decay), and a fast path that avoids heap allocations. Also consider approximate counters (decaying window) to reduce contention.

Simon Loe: Telemetry requirements: emit served_fraction, fairness_ratio (observed/expected), bias_cap_value, and starvation_incidents. Add an alert if served_fraction < min_share for >5m or if fairness_ratio < 0.7 for >10m. These will let us catch regression before customers notice.

Nina Ortega: Rollout plan suggestion: 1) shadow mode for 48h; 2) 1% canary traffic for 6h measuring fairness metrics + p95/p99 latency; 3) 5% canary 24h; 4) ramp with abort criteria. Also include cost delta target (<=3% token-cost increase).

Maria Chen: Action items: I'll write the RFC follow-up with the hybrid algorithm and telemetry contract. @Ajay Patel can you prototype the sampler (perf microbench + approximate counters)? @policy-bot please run param sweep on bias_cap=0.0..0.5 and min_share=0.01..0.1 and post results.

policy-bot: job queued: fallback-bias-sweep (bias_cap sweep + min_share grid). Expected runtime ~3h. Will post summary when done.

Ajay Patel: Sounds good — I'll start a perf branch tomorrow and add a simple in-memory sampler for microbenching. :thumbsup:

Maria Chen: Thanks — we'll sync in the architecture sync on Friday to pick thresholds and finalize rollout checklist.
